page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7t.6xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance based on the KVM hypervisor architecture. It features 24 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped across 12 physical cores and 24 threads from an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The x86_64 CPU configuration includes 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of shared L3 cache. It incorporates advanced vector instructions including AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI, along with hardware cryptography accelerations like AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

System memory is provisioned at 48.0 GB, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Benchmark data shows large-block memory read bandwidth reaching 129.2 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 62.95 GB/sec, while cached small-block reads reach 1266.21 GB/sec. The instance delivers a PassMark memory score of 2334.21 and a multi-core PassMark CPU score of 29499.47, reflecting consistent multi-threaded compute performance across enterprise integer and floating-point tasks.

The instance does not include bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes for persistent data. Hardware networking features a baseline bandwidth of 12 Gbps without default complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Dedicated compute power translates to 23.57 million Redis SET operations per second and a static web serving throughput of 27.72 GB/sec. In AI inference tasks, text generation with small 135M parameter models demonstrates upper-quartile throughput at 295.58 tokens per second.

Given its compute density and lack of native local disks, ecs.c7t.6xlarge offers qualitative efficiency for compute-heavy workloads where execution speed takes precedence over large working sets in RAM. The instance is suited for batch processing, web serving tiers, software compilation, ETL pipelines, and lightweight CPU-based inference workloads.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7t.6xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by a 2.7 GHz Intel Xeon 8369B processor. It provides 24 dedicated vCPUs (12 physical cores with hyperthreading) and 48.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 1:2 core-to-memory profile. Vector extensions such as AVX-512 and cryptographic accelerators are present. The instance does not bundle local storage, relying entirely on network-attached storage, and provides a 12 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic benchmarks indicate solid multi-core performance, recording 12002.0 in Geekbench multi-core and 29499.47 in PassMark CPU tests. Memory benchmarks show 129.2 GB/sec uncached read throughput. This server type fits compute-intensive workloads that require sustained processor execution without extensive memory capacity, such as web application servers, data transformation tasks, build farms, and microservices.
